As demonstrated in Table 2, our method impressively improves the success rate of GUI low-level tasks for 3B and 7B models, with the average success rate increasing from 55.65 to 80.88 at the 3B scale. Compared to UI-R1 [9], which is concurrent work also trained using RFT, our model achieves a 10-point improvement at the 3B scale, validating that RL training focused on high-level tasks can further enhance the model's understanding of low-level instructions. Note that an interesting observation is that the use of small-scale SFT data even leads to performance degradation on some metrics such as GR on AndroidControl-Low. This limitation stems from SFT's reliance on taskspecific labeled data, which constrains the model's ability to adapt to unseen environments

OmniAct-Desktop is used to test low-level task execution on desktop platforms. As demonstrated in Table 2, our method impressively improves the success rate of GUI low-level tasks for 3B and 7B models, with the average success rate increasing from 55.65 to 80.88 at the 3B scale. Compared to UI-R1 [9], which is concurrent work also trained using RFT, our model achieves a 10-point improvement at the 3B scale, validating that RL training focused on high-level tasks can further enhance the model's understanding of low-level instructions. Note that an interesting observation is that the use of small-scale SFT data even leads to performance degradation on some metrics such as GR on AndroidControl-Low. This limitation stems from SFT's reliance on taskspecific labeled data, which constrains the model's ability to adapt to unseen environments
